CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFOBJECT

CFOBJECT loads a Java class into the KoldFusion Java Virtual Machine and stores it in a variable, so you can call its methods and read and set its public fields with ordinary CFML: obj.method(args), obj.field, <CFSET obj.field = value>. On ColdFusion for Windows NT it also creates COM objects and connects to CORBA servers; KoldFusion for UNIX has no COM subsystem and no CORBA ORB, so those types raise an error of type Object.

Category

Extensibility

Syntax

<CFOBJECT TYPE="JAVA"
    ACTION="Create"
    CLASS="java_class_name"
    NAME="object_name">

<CFOBJECT TYPE="COM"
    ACTION="Create/Connect"
    CLASS="program_id"
    NAME="object_name"
    CONTEXT="InProc/Local/Remote"
    SERVER="server_name">

<CFOBJECT TYPE="CORBA"
    CONTEXT="IOR/NameService"
    CLASS="file_or_naming_service"
    NAME="object_name"
    LOCALE="type-value arguments">

Attributes

TYPE
Optional, default "COM". Kind of object: JAVA, COM or CORBA.
ACTION
Required for JAVA and COM. "Create" loads the class (Java) or makes a new object (COM); "Connect" attaches to a running COM server.
CLASS
Required. Java: the full class name, such as "java.util.Hashtable" (case sensitive; slashes work too: "java/util/Hashtable"). COM: the ProgID. CORBA: the IOR file or the naming service path.
NAME
Required. Variable that receives the object.
CONTEXT
Optional. COM: InProc, Local or Remote. CORBA (required): IOR or NameService.
SERVER
Optional. COM server name for CONTEXT="Remote".
LOCALE
Optional. CORBA: arguments for the ORB's init_orb(), each starting with a hyphen.

Usage

Java objects

CFOBJECT loads the class but does not construct it yet, so static methods and fields can be used straight away. Call init() to run a constructor with arguments; otherwise the first instance method call (or instance field access) runs the constructor that takes no arguments:

<CFOBJECT TYPE="JAVA" ACTION="Create" CLASS="java.lang.StringBuffer" NAME="Buf">
<CFSET Buf.init("Hello")>              <!--- new StringBuffer("Hello") --->
<CFSET Buf.append(", world")>

Method and field names are not case sensitive; class names are. Overloaded methods are chosen by the number of arguments and then by how well the CFML values fit the parameter types; when that is ambiguous, say which Java type you mean with JavaCast. Strings, numbers, booleans and dates are converted both ways; a CFML array becomes a java.util.Vector (or a Java array, if the method wants one) and a structure a java.util.Hashtable. Values returned by Java come back as CFML values: strings, numbers, booleans, dates, and arrays (from Java arrays, Vectors and other Lists) or structures (from Hashtables and other Maps); any other object stays a Java object you can call. A Java char comes back as its character code; use Chr() to show it.

A Java exception becomes a CFML error of type Object, whose CFCATCH.Message is the exception's class name and CFCATCH.Detail its message. GetException(object) returns the exception object itself.

Classes are found in the java/classes directory of the KoldFusion installation, in cfx.jar, in the Java runtime, and on the Class Path set on the Java page of the Administrator. The Java Virtual Machine is loaded the first time a page needs it; if none is installed, the tag raises an error of type Object.

Note  ColdFusion 4.5 released objects at the end of each page. KoldFusion also lets you keep a Java object in the Session, Application or Server scope: the stored copy refers to the same Java object, which stays alive as long as that scope does. Several requests can then use it at the same time, so lock it with CFLOCK (or use a thread-safe class such as java.util.Hashtable). Java objects cannot be stored in Client variables or serialized with CFWDDX.

COM and CORBA

COM is a Windows technology, and the Java runtimes of today no longer include a CORBA ORB (Java IDL was removed in Java 11), so on KoldFusion these always fail with an error of type Object. Wrap such code in CFTRY so a page written for the Windows server degrades gracefully.

CFOBJECT and CreateObject can be disabled in the Administrator (Basic Security, Tag Restrictions); a restricted tag raises a security error instead.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- A Hashtable from the Java runtime, used straight from CFML --->
<CFTRY>
  <CFOBJECT TYPE="JAVA" ACTION="Create" CLASS="java.util.Hashtable" NAME="Prices">
  <CFSET Prices.put("56K modem", "129.95")>
  <CFSET Prices.put("Zip drive", "149.00")>
  <CFSET Prices.put("Y2K sticker", "0.99")>
  <CFOUTPUT>
  <P>The Hashtable holds #Prices.size()# items. A Zip drive costs
  #DollarFormat(Prices.get("Zip drive"))#.</P>
  </CFOUTPUT>
  <!--- returned Hashtables become structures --->
  <CFSET Copy = Prices.clone()>
  <TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
  <CFLOOP COLLECTION="#Copy#" ITEM="Item">
    <CFOUTPUT><TR><TD>#Item#</TD><TD ALIGN=RIGHT>#Copy[Item]#</TD></TR></CFOUTPUT>
  </CFLOOP>
  </TABLE>
  <!--- static methods work before init() --->
  <CFOBJECT TYPE="JAVA" ACTION="Create" CLASS="java.lang.Math" NAME="JMath">
  <CFOUTPUT><P>Math.max(1999, 2000) = #JMath.max(1999, 2000)#,
  Math.PI = #JMath.PI#</P></CFOUTPUT>
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Object">
    <CFOUTPUT>
    <P><B>No Java today:</B> #CFCATCH.Message#<BR>
    <I>#CFCATCH.Detail#</I></P>
    </CFOUTPUT>
  </CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
